newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks erase gains in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks erase gains in volatile trade.

text.p: Spanish stocks pared gains on Thursday in volatile trade, with investors taking profits to secure earnings before heading off on summer vacations.
"The market is volatile and it wouldn't surprise me if it fell, depending on other European markets," a fund manager said.
A trader at a Spanish bank added, "It's calm. The market has gone up a lot and now there is profit-taking.
The Ibex-35 was down 10.57 points, 0.15 percent, to 7,125.56 having opened at 7,188.17. The general index was up 1.25 points, or 0.20 percent to 626.77 at mid-session.
Stocks fell further after JP Morgan said it was downgrading its Spanish weighting to neutral from overweight.
"The market is entering a possible correction phase with the Ibex offering strong resistance above 7,150 points," another dealer in Madrid said.

"Also the change in Morgan's view had its effect," another dealer said. Earlier on Thursday, JP Morgan Securities Ltd said it was dowgrading the Spanish equity market to neutral from overweight due to more limited upside to earnings forecasts.

Telefonica lost 120 pesetas to 4,315, while Repsol was down 60 to 6,510, but BCH outperformed the market gaining 0.82 percent or 50 pesetas to 6,150 pesetas on talk it would soon approve a share split.
